articles.text:
Business & Markets
Blue J Announces $176M in Funding at $700M Valuation to Scale AI Tax Research Agent
By James Dargan · 12 November 2026 · 1 min read
Toronto-based Blue J, which builds AI software for tax research, has secured US$176 million in a round led by Baltimore’s JMI Equity, valuing the company at US$700 million. Existing investors Oak HC/FT, Sapphire Ventures and Intrepid Growth Partners also took part.
Nearly US$100 million will go towards buying shares from employees and early investors, with the remaining US$80 million funding the commercialisation of Blue J’s new agent product and expansion into the UK, its third market after the US and Canada.
Founded in 2015 by University of Toronto law professor Benjamin Alarie and two colleagues, Blue J answers complex tax questions in seconds with source citations. Alarie rebuilt the product around large language models after ChatGPT arrived in 2022, and says accuracy has risen from roughly 50% in early versions to more than 95%.
The deal comes just over a year after a US$122 million round in August 2025. Recurring revenue has since grown 165% to the mid-eight-figure range, and client firms have increased from fewer than 100 three years ago to more than 6,500.
JMI principal Jack Duane said the firm had tracked Blue J for years, heard strongly positive customer feedback and considers the product extremely difficult to replicate thanks to its proprietary data and domain expertise.

Ondas Posts Record $167.5 Million Q3 Revenue, Raises 2026 Outlook
1 min read
ONDS
Ondas reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $167.5 million, up 100% sequentially and more than 16-fold year over year. Gross profit was $36.5 million, with a GAAP gross margin of 21.8%, while net loss was $64.7 million. The company raised its 2026 revenue target to at least $550 million and initiated a 2027 target of at least $1.1 billion.
Financial Highlights
Revenue was $167.5 million, compared with $10.1 million in Q3 2025 and $83.8 million in Q2 2026; pro forma organic revenue grew 64% year over year.
Gross profit was $36.5 million, compared with $2.6 million a year earlier. GAAP gross margin was 21.8%, and adjusted gross profit and adjusted gross margin were $58.3 million and 34.8%, respectively.
Operating loss was $189.5 million, compared with $15.5 million in Q3 2025.
Net loss was $64.7 million, compared with $7.5 million in Q3 2025. Diluted loss per share was $0.10.
Adjusted EBITDA loss was $59.7 million, compared with $8.1 million in Q3 2025. Ondas expects operating-platform Adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026 and company-wide profitability by Q3 2027.
Business Highlights
Formed Ondas Sentinel, combining DZYNE Technologies and World View under unified leadership to advance U.S. defense programs and the development, production, and deployment of defense technologies.
Established Regna AI to develop sovereign AI applications for defense and national security customers, using NVIDIA Nemotron models and Palantir platforms.
Expanded its land-systems portfolio and capabilities through acquisitions spanning unmanned ground vehicles, precision strike, sensing, connectivity, and navigation. The company also plans to acquire Stemme to strengthen production capacity for the ULTRA aircraft.
Advanced customer programs and product deployments, including counter-drone protection at major sports venues, a U.S. Army follow-on task order, the Digital Bat program, and the first flight of Blitz Block 3. Ondas also opened a training, testing, and flight-operations hub in Springfield, Ohio.
Original SEC Filing: Ondas Inc. [ ONDS ] - 8-K - Nov. 12, 2026

articles.text:
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 11:44 AM
MaxCyte: $151.8 Million Akron Bio Acquisition Expands Cell Therapy Platform
MaxCyte has agreed to acquire Akron BioProducts from affiliates of Arcline Investment Management for $151.8 million. The transaction is expected to close before the end of 2026, subject to customary conditions.
Akron Bio supplies Good Manufacturing Practice-grade reagents and ancillary materials used across cell therapy manufacturing. Its products include cytokines, growth factors, human plasma-derived materials, specialty media, and other consumables.
The acquisition will expand MaxCyte beyond its historical focus on nonviral cell engineering. Akron’s products are used in both viral and nonviral workflows at stages ranging from cell expansion through cryopreservation.
The combined company’s technologies are incorporated into five commercially approved therapies and support more than 100 clinical programs. Both businesses maintain drug master files referenced in customers’ regulatory submissions, creating long-term connections to validated manufacturing processes.
Akron is expected to produce approximately $28 million in 2026 revenue and between $7 million and $8 million of EBITDA. MaxCyte expects the acquisition to nearly double its revenue base, increase recurring consumables revenue, and accelerate its path toward profitability.
The companies have limited customer overlap despite serving similar biopharmaceutical markets. MaxCyte therefore expects to use its commercial infrastructure to introduce Akron products to additional customers and pursue cross-selling opportunities.
The buyer projects that Akron’s positive cash flow will help reduce the combined company’s annual cash burn to less than $10 million in 2027. MaxCyte expects to hold approximately $40 million to $45 million of cash when the transaction closes.
The consideration consists of $105 million in cash, subject to adjustments, 20,639,733 MaxCyte shares valued at approximately $26.8 million, and $20 million of guaranteed deferred payments. The deferred amount will be paid in two $10 million installments in January 2028 and January 2029.
MaxCyte has also secured a credit facility of up to $75 million from MidCap Financial, consisting of a $55 million term loan and a $20 million revolver. It plans to draw $20 million from the term loan and $2 million from the revolver at closing.
Akron will continue operating under its existing brand, with its management team and employees remaining part of the combined organization.
KEY QUOTES
“The acquisition of Akron marks an exciting new chapter for MaxCyte. This acquisition represents a significant step forward for us, expanding our presence across the viral and non-viral cell therapy development and manufacturing workflow, while projecting to nearly double our revenue base and accelerate our path to profitability. From day one, Akron provides us with an established portfolio of clinical and commercial programs supported by Akron’s DMFs and reagents. By bringing together two highly complementary businesses, we are diversifying our revenue base, increasing our mix of recurring revenue and expanding our exposure to the growth of commercially approved cell therapies, positioning MaxCyte for more durable near- and long-term growth. articles.title: Addex Spin-out Neurosterix Closes $105 Million Series B Financing
articles.snippet: Addex Spin-out Neurosterix Closes $105 Million Series B Financing GlobeNewswire
articles.text:
Ad Hoc Announcement Pursuant to Art. 53 LR
Geneva, Switzerland, November 11, 2026 - Addex Therapeutics (SIX and Nasdaq: ADXN), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders, today announced that its spin-out company, Neurosterix, has closed a $105 million Series B financing from a syndicate of leading life science investors. Addex did not participate in the financing and its equity interest now represents 8.5% of the issued capital at a valuation of $18.6 million.
The proceeds raised will support mainly the planned Phase 2 clinical development of NTX-253, a highly selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator (PAM), for schizophrenia. The financing will also support Neurosterix’s broader pipeline of selective allosteric modulators for a range of neuropsychiatric disorders.
“The closing of this significant financing is a huge endorsement of the allosteric approach pioneered by Addex in schizophrenia as well as other neuropsychiatric disorders. Congatulations to the whole Neurosterix team, which has made enormous strides in advancing lead program NTX-253 through clinical development and ready for Phase 2, following our spin-out in 2024,” said Tim Dyer, CEO of Addex.
About NTX-253 and M4 PAMs
The M4 muscarinic receptor is a validated target for treating schizophrenia and related disorders through indirect modulation of dopamine signaling. NTX-253 is a potent, highly selective, oral PAM of M4 that fine-tunes muscarinic signaling in the brain to potentially reduce psychosis symptoms while avoiding the movement disorders and metabolic complications associated with traditional dopamine antagonists. Neurosterix has completed Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose clinical studies of NTX-253, which data supporting advancing into larger scale Phase 2 clinical studies.
About Neurosterix
Neurosterix is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on transforming neuropsychiatric care through selective allosteric modulation. The company’s approach is designed to fine-tune brain signaling with greater precision and selectivity, with the goal of developing safer, more effective treatments for people living with schizophrenia, and mood and anxiety disorders. Neurosterix’s pipeline includes NTX-253, a selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator (PAM) for schizophrenia; NTX-819, a potentially first-in-class mGlu7 negative allosteric modulator (NAM) for mood and anxiety disorders; and NTX-529, a second differentiated M4 PAM for additional psychosis- and mood-related disorders. Neurosterix has operations in Boston and Geneva. For more information, visit www.neurosterix.com.
About Addex Therapeutics
Addex Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders. Addex's lead drug candidate, dipraglurant (mGlu5 negative allosteric modulator or NAM), is under evaluation for future development in brain injury recovery, including post-stroke and traumatic brain injury recovery. Addex has selected a GABAB PAM drug candidate for development in substance use disorders and has successfully completed IND enabling studies. In addition, Addex is advancing a differentiated GABAB PAM compound for the treatment of chronic cough. Clara Raises $105 Million to Grow Latin American Corporate Spend Management Platform
By Julie Muhn (@julieschicktanz) Posted on November 13, 2026
Categories: Daily news , Funding
Clara raised $105 million, comprising a $65 million Series C equity round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility, bringing its total debt and equity funding to $838 million.
Clara will use the funding to expand its market reach and enhance its AI capabilities, including its MCP integration that enables AI agents to access financial data and execute authorized transactions.
The funding comes amid global growth in corporate card and spend management platforms, as providers expand beyond payments and expense tracking to offer integrated, AI-powered financial management tools.
Brazil-based spend management platform Clara raised $105 million this week. The round is comprised of $65 million in equity in a Series C round and the renewal of a $40 million growth financing facility from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF).
The $65 million Series C was anchored by Citius, Kaszek, and DEG, a subsidiary of Germany’s KfW Group. The round also attracted participation from 10 existing investors and three new investors, including CMT Digital and Nascent VC.
The latest investment brings Clara’s total debt and equity funding to $838 million, following several debt financing deals over the past year. In November 2025, Clara secured $70 million in structured debt financing from BBVA Spark, Covalto, and the International Finance Corporation (IFC). Three months later, the company renewed a $150 million credit facility with Goldman Sachs, bringing its total debt capacity to more than $250 million.
Clara will use today’s funding to expand its go-to-market team and strengthen the automation and AI capabilities of its platform. Clara was founded in 2020 and now helps more than 45,000 businesses automate routine work, control spending, and make better financial decisions. The company’s platform offers corporate cards, bill payments, spend management, accounts payable, and accounts receivable to help businesses make and manage payments. Along with the financing announcement, Clara said it has also surpassed $100 million in annualized net revenue and maintained positive EBITDA for more than a year.
Among Clara’s capabilities is its Model Context Protocol (MCP) integration, which connects the platform with AI agents to enable customers to access real-time spending reports and forecasts using natural language, as well as execute authorized transactions autonomously. The company also offers AI-powered policy enforcement that checks employee expenses against company policies in real time, global spend management tools that allow businesses to manage expenses across countries and currencies, and fleet management solutions that support fuel payments and vehicle operations.
“Clara exists to champion Latin American businesses, and we work tirelessly to give them the tools to compete and win on the global stage,” said Clara Co-Founder and CEO Gerry Giacomán Colyer. “The region has long been underserved by financial platforms designed for other markets. We’re combining AI with local expertise to solve challenges specific to doing business here and give our customers a distinct competitive edge.”

articles.text:
Databento Raises $100 Million Series C at $1.1 Billion Valuation
News provided by
Databento Inc.
Nov 12, 2026, 08:57 ET
Share this article
Share this article
SALT LAKE CITY , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Databento, the market data platform for modern finance, today announced a $100 million Series C financing at a $1.1 billion valuation. The round was led by Fifth Down Capital, an early investor in Databento, with participation from nearly all of the company's existing investors, including NEA, DRW Venture Capital, Tribe Capital, and Hedosophia.
The announcement follows Databento's $97 million Series B earlier this year. Since closing its previous round, the company has more than doubled its revenue while remaining profitable.
Databento serves leading quantitative trading firms, brokerages, asset managers, commodities firms, and digital asset companies. The company has also established a strong presence in artificial intelligence, having signed enterprise contracts with five of the six leading frontier AI labs.
Databento had 39 employees when it closed its Series C, reaching a $1.1 billion valuation with a fraction of the headcount of traditional market data providers.
"In this AI era, we're seeing remarkably small teams build billion-dollar companies, but that level of efficiency is unprecedented in the market data industry," said Christina Qi, co-founder and CEO of Databento. "Until now, reaching this milestone required hundreds of employees given the sheer scale of physical infrastructure involved. I'm incredibly proud of what we've accomplished, and we'll continue to prioritize exceptional talent as we grow."
"Fifth Down first invested in Databento pre-revenue, as we recognized early on that the company had an opportunity to challenge the established model for delivering financial market data," said Andrew Spellman, founder and CEO of Fifth Down Capital. "Our confidence has only grown as Databento's traction and execution have demonstrated it can serve demanding institutional customers, sustain rapid growth, and build a profitable business. Databento's performance has reinforced our original thesis and strengthened our conviction in the company. We are thankful to Christina and Luca for the opportunity to increase our investment and involvement by leading the Series C financing."
The round also included a strategic investment from Fitch Ventures, bringing the perspective of a leading financial information provider with deep expertise in credit ratings, financial data, and market insights.
"Financial data is becoming increasingly API-driven and machine-consumed, creating an opportunity to fundamentally rethink how institutions and other market participants access it," said Gabby Munoz, Global Head of M&A and Venture Investments at Fitch Group. "Databento has built differentiated infrastructure at the source and paired it with a modern, self-service model that makes institutional-grade market data available on demand. We're excited to back the team as they scale a platform we believe will help shape how market data is captured, delivered, and consumed."
The new funding will support Databento's continued investment in its market data infrastructure and expansion into additional asset classes.
